transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Luis Martinez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (NexaHealth CTO); Samir Patel (Nexa DevOps); Kara Nguyen (Nexa Product); Maya Singh (Nexa Security); Ben Carter (Nexa Data Eng)

Summary (auto): quick onboarding check, access/VPC status, benchmark plan for latency and cost, tune recommendations (batching/quant), security checklist and next steps.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone uh thanks for joining, appreciate zooming in early. can folks hear me okay?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: yeah we can hear you, thanks Alex. morning from SF.
[00:08] Alex Chen: cool. quick agenda — onboarding progress, access and VPC peering, run cadence for the benchmark, tuning knobs we want to try (batching, quant, prefix cache), and then next steps.
[00:20] Priya Rao: i'll jump in on the technical bits; last week we requested the VPC peering details and an S3 bucket with sample evals.
[00:28] Samir Patel: sorry, yeah, schedule slipped a bit — we're finalizing the subnet CIDRs now. i'll have the peering ticket after lunch.
[00:35] Kara Nguyen: just to clarify — we want both throughput and tail latency on case mix, right? not just average.
[00:40] Alex Chen: exactly, kara. tail p95/p99 matter for user experience.
[00:44] Ben Carter: i've uploaded a 500-request sample to the s3 path we talked about, but i think the filename might have weird casing, so check the bucket. link is in chat.
[00:52] Priya Rao: perfect ben, we'll pick that up. quick note — when you upload please include the expected prompt length distribution, that helps with kernel selection.
[01:00] Jordan Lee: on security, maya is here, do you have any red flags?
[01:03] Maya Singh: a couple of items — we need KMS integration, audit log retention, and SSO/SAML for RBAC. also SOC2 type II evidence is a must before prod.
[01:14] Luis Martinez: we have a security appendix we can send, and redwood supports KMS + customer-managed keys for private deployments. we'll send the SOC2 artifacts link after the call.
[01:24] Jordan Lee: good. cost is also a blocker for us — we need an estimate for hosted vs dedicated.
[01:30] Alex Chen: understood. i'll share a baseline cost model — for the staged 50k token run we'll include per-token cost and projected monthly burn for the expected throughput.
[01:38] Samir Patel: about the VPC approach, we prefer private deployment but for the POC we can do dedicated capacity in a VPC peered mode, does that match?
[01:46] Priya Rao: yes, you can do Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering. technically the control plane stays in cloud but data flows in the peered private network. small note — we sometimes see MTU or route table issues during peering, so double-check routes.
[01:59] Alex Chen: Priya, can you outline the exact IAM role and ports we need?
[02:03] Priya Rao: sure — outbound HTTPS for control plane, then custom CIDR pairs for internal traffic; we'll send a checklist. also need an IAM role with s3:GetObject for the eval data and the ability to create Cloudwatch log streams if you want logs forwarded.
[02:18] Samir Patel: okay i'll add those to the ticket.
[02:21] Ben Carter: one more, we're using a model that typically runs with 2k context, but some prompts are 8k. how does Redwood handle variable sequence lengths?
[02:30] Priya Rao: runtime picks kernels based on observed sequence length distribution; for mixed workloads we recommend prefix caching for long contexts plus dynamic batching. quantization profiles can help reduce memory and cost but may impact a bit of accuracy — we can run AB tests.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: can you give us an example trade-off? like if we quantize to 4-bit what's the latency and quality change.
[02:52] Priya Rao: ballpark — 4-bit often reduces memory by ~2-2.5x and can reduce p50 latency by ~10-20% on GPU infer; quality delta depends on model, usually small on instruction following but we should validate on your eval set.
[03:06] Kara Nguyen: we'd want to preserve key patient-safety prompts, so any quality regressions need to be measured.
[03:11] Alex Chen: totally. that's why the benchmark will include safety-critical prompt subset.
[03:16] Luis Martinez: also FYI Redwood Optimize suggestions will flag recommended batching and quant profiles after the run.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: what about fallbacks? say traffic spikes or a node goes down. do you have graceful degradation?
[03:28] Priya Rao: yes — smart routing can fallback to other model variants or different capacity tiers; for strict SLOs we can configure a canary and automatic fallback policy.
[03:36] Maya Singh: is there an audit trail for those fallbacks? we need logs for incident review.
[03:41] Luis Martinez: audit logs are retained and we can forward to your SIEM; retention length is configurable as an add-on.
[03:47] Samir Patel: back on access — who should we expect to see the peering request from? redwood account or a partner?
[03:53] Alex Chen: you'll see an automated peering from Redwood Dedicated — the ticket will come from infra@redwood.ai but it will contain the peer CIDRs and contact.
[04:00] Ben Carter: small nit — earlier you mentioned KV cache, but we call it Kay-Vee cache in docs sometimes and that confused our interns.
[04:07] Priya Rao: yeah we see that in transcripts a lot — KV cache = key-value cache, prefix caching is what helps for repeated contexts.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: ok next, timeline — we want bench results by mid next week, is that feasible?
[04:16] Priya Rao: if we get the eval dataset and peering info this week, yes. timing: staging run takes a day, analysis another day, so mid-next-week is realistic.
[04:24] Alex Chen: i'll mark deliverables — Alex will send pricing + benchmark sheet by Friday (2027-08-06), Priya will run the 50k token latency/cost run and share logs, Samir will give peering and IAM details by Thursday (08-05), Ben will confirm the S3 path.
[04:40] Kara Nguyen: customers often ask about sample throughput numbers — can you show a small table in the spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens?
[04:47] Alex Chen: yes, will include that.
[04:50] Maya Singh: one more security Q — does Redwood support customer-managed HSM for encryption keys?
[04:55] Luis Martinez: yes we support KMS + options for HSM with Private deployments. we'll include a note in the security appendix.
[05:02] Jordan Lee: ok sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:06] Alex Chen: none; main blocker is the VPC details and the sample eval set — once we have those, we can run the benchmark.
[05:12] Ben Carter: i'll double-check the S3 object names and resend a link.
[05:15] Samir Patel: i'll open the peering ticket after stand and ping you.
[05:18] Alex Chen: great — last thing, i'll also include a short runbook for the POC steps and a link to our dedicated deployment checklist: https://redwood.ai/ops/dedicated-checklist (doc link).
[05:28] Jordan Lee: thanks all.
[05:30] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and circle back same time next week. bye.

Recorded action items and next steps are in the metadata. Transcript may contain mis-hearings and abbreviated technical terms; please refer to the attached security appendix and benchmark template that Alex will send.
